question_title: Who will win the 2026 Tennessee Democratic gubernatorial primary?
summary: Jerri Green is the dominant frontrunner in the August 6, 2026 Tennessee Democratic gubernatorial primary — the only elected official in the field, with a ~13x fundraising lead ($703K), a lead in the only public poll (Green 14%, McCants 11%), and prediction market pricing near 94%. I discount the market to ~80% to reflect the 62% undecided share in a low-information, crowded field where Tennessee's disproportionately Black Democratic primary electorate could break toward McCants or Atwater in ways not captured by fundraising. McCants (close poll second) and Atwater (prior statewide/mayoral candidate) absorb most of the residual probability; Cyr, Kurtz, and write-ins are negligible.

resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the candidate declared the winner of the Democratic primary for Governor of Tennessee, held August 6, 2026, based on the official certified results reported by the Tennessee Secretary of State's election results portal (https://sos.tn.gov/elections) or, before certification, by the Associated Press or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The winner is the candidate who receives the most votes (Tennessee primaries are decided by plurality, not a majority). It resolves "Any other candidate" if the winner is a write-in candidate or anyone not listed among the named options.
fine_print: The five named candidates certified to the August 6, 2026 Democratic gubernatorial primary ballot are Carnita Atwater, Tim Cyr, Jerri Green, Adam "Ditch" Kurtz, and Kevin Lee McCants. In the event of an exact tie for first place resolved by a subsequent procedure (e.g., recount or drawing of lots) under Tennessee law, the question resolves to the candidate ultimately certified as the nominee.

revision_history.reviewer_assessment:
I verified every factor against the research trace and found no fabrication, double-counting, or wrong-direction errors. The probability is well-calibrated.

RESOLUTION CRITERIA: Fully provided in the question (SoS portal / AP, plurality wins, 5 named candidates, "Any other candidate" for write-ins). Not MISSING, so no Metaculus recovery was required. Factors and probabilities map correctly to the criteria — all five named candidates plus "Any other candidate" are enumerated, and the plurality rule is respected.

PROBABILITY ASSESSMENT: The agent moved from market (Green 94 / Atwater 6 / McCants <1) to Green 80 / McCants 8 / Atwater 7. This redistribution is coherent and defensible:
1. Discounting Green 94→80% is justified — the market is stale (April), thin (~$90K volume), and 62% of voters are undecided in a low-info race. 80% is if anything mildly conservative for a candidate leading every fundamental.
2. Raising McCants above the market's <1% is grounded in the poll (11%, only 3pp behind Green, within MOE), not pure narrative — so 8% is a reasonable synthesis of poll + market.
My own independent estimate lands very close: Green ~75-85%, with McCants and Atwater each ~5-10%. No meaningful divergence.

ANCHOR: The stated anchor is the market (94%); the 14pp departure to 80% is warranted by stale/thin market data plus a live 62%-undecided poll — a concrete, verified basis, not narrative accumulation.

COUNTERARGUMENT: Substantive, not a token gesture — it builds a coherent alternative (heavily-Black Memphis/urban electorate consolidating behind McCants/Atwater, MOE overlap, stale market) and states concrete disconfirming evidence that would change its mind. Confidence 0.72 appropriately reflects the thin single-poll evidence base and stale market.
